drills.q: Write the skeleton of an ask paragraph: what six elements?
drills.a: Decision + resource + duration + deadline + default-if-silent + what-no-means. Example: 'Approve 1 engineer and $3K/mo inference for 6 weeks to validate AI hints against our eval gate; decide by Friday; silence = no; a no costs a quarter of learning and we revisit with vendor data.'

drills.q: Name the eight blocks of a fundable one-pager in order.
drills.a: Decision requested (size/deadline/default) -> problem+why-now -> evidence (2-3 sourced numbers) -> cheapest path -> value band vs cost band -> alternatives incl. do-nothing -> top-3 risks x mitigations -> kill condition. ~450-600 words.

drills.q: Your value model: low $150K, mid $400K, high $800K/yr; cost $315K. How do you frame the ask?
drills.a: Tranche it: ~3 x $105K with re-up gates ('evidence >= X% of midpoint before tranche two'), payback ~9.5 months at midpoint, and show whether the case survives pessimistic-value x doubled-cost. '$105K buys the next proof point; stop-loss defined' beats one faith-based ask.

drills.q: CFO challenges your churn assumption mid-meeting. Walk the live response.
drills.a: Don't defend - recompute together on their input; state whether the decision flips. Survives: 'even at your churn we clear cost.' Doesn't: 'your churn is exactly why tranche-one gates exist - we learn cheaply before most spend.' If you can't recompute live, commit to the sensitivity table within 24-48h and deliver.

drills.q: Sequence the pre-alignment work for a controversial platform consolidation.
drills.a: Stakeholder map -> socialize problem statement in 1:1s incorporating feedback visibly -> skeptic preview ('what would kill this?') -> their objection answered IN doc with credit -> final >=48h ahead, comments open -> meeting on unresolved threads only -> explicit decision/owner/date. Roughly 60% of influence happens before anyone sees the doc.

drills.q: 'Great doc, wrong quarter.' What do you do in the next 48 hours?
drills.a: Ask 'what would need to be true for Q2?'; classify capacity vs priority vs slow-no; shrink tranche to fit discretionary space or attach to blocker's metric; set dated follow-up; ship cheapest unblockable slice generating evidence so next cycle arrives with data instead of the same slide.

drills.q: Your funded project missed its promised band. What do you send leadership?
drills.a: Actuals-vs-promise report within the quarter, unprompted: which assumption failed, what was learned, remaining runway decision recommendation (kill per pre-registered condition or pivot). Honest misses compound credibility fastest; defending zombies burns budget AND reputation.

drills.q: Write for executives who give docs 90 seconds: five mechanics plus the test.
drills.a: Ask+stakes inside 50 words; one-screen self-sufficiency; assertion-headings carrying conclusions; numbers as tables; hedges killed. Test: hand to an outsider for 90 seconds - can they state ask/stakes/deadline? Failure means revise, not explain.

drills.q: A peer agrees in 1:1s then torpedoes your proposals publicly. Full playbook.
drills.a: Verify pattern (minutes); take objections seriously enough to write down; circulate earlier with written-dissent deadlines; in-meeting redirect: 'that's addressed page two - which test does the mitigation fail?'; one direct private relationship conversation if persistent; escalation reserved for genuine bad faith. Going around them converts a peer into an enemy with receipts.

drills.q: When is acting WITHOUT a document the right call?
drills.a: Reversible two-way-door decisions inside your authority (experiment flags, bounded tooling trials): act, document outcomes after. Emergencies invert the pipeline. Boundary test: state which door you're walking through BEFORE walking through it - decisiveness is acting inside mandate and reporting; process-violation is acting outside mandate regardless of outcome quality.
